Well, I'll tell you how I'm thinking about this year. I've only been farming these 5 mu for three years now — before that I was doing other work — so I still watch what my neighbors do pretty closely. The old man next to my plot, he's been doing wheat-maize here for thirty years, so I mostly follow what he does and adjust a little.

**Wheat (winter crop):**
Last year I got about 400 kg per mu, which wasn't bad. I planted around October 10th, same as most folks in the village. This year I'll do about the same. I buy regular seed from the agricultural supply shop — not the fancy hybrid, the regular kind, costs maybe 5 yuan per mu worth. I put down compound fertilizer before planting, about two bags for my whole 5 mu (that's the 15-15-15 kind, maybe 40 kg per mu of the compound), and then I topdress with urea around jointing time in spring, maybe half a bag per mu. My neighbor says you need to water at jointing and again at heading, so I do that — two waterings usually, three if spring is dry. The well pumping costs money so I don't overdo it. I spray for weeds once in spring, that's it for pesticide usually unless I see aphids.

**Maize (summer crop):**
Right after wheat harvest in mid-June, I need to plant maize fast — my wife and I do it together, sometimes my older brother helps. No time to plow properly, I just direct-seed into the wheat stubble. I hire the neighbor's small planter for a day, costs me maybe 30 yuan per mu. Seed is hybrid, I buy fresh every year because that's what everyone says to do — about 40 yuan per mu. I put fertilizer in with the planter, compound again, then topdress urea when the maize is about knee-high. Last year I didn't irrigate the maize because rain was okay, but if July is dry I'll water once. Got about 450 kg per mu last year.

**My thinking on cash:**
Money is tight. With 5 mu I'm not getting rich from farming — my brother-in-law works construction in Handan and that's most of our cash income. I keep fertilizer to what I can afford without borrowing. If the wheat price is bad at harvest I might hold some grain instead of selling right away.
